proposed_from.topic: Matched honest nuclear-radius frontier for staggered low-rank panels under iid noise: under fixed deterministic adoption, known fixed rank, iid Gaussian cell errors, normalized strong-factor/incoherence bounds, and quantitative overlap Grams, define the minimax expected observable nuclear-error radius over all uniformly honest procedures. Characterize it up to constants with a polynomial-time wedge-aware spectral certificate and a same-class all-procedure lower bound; keep the exact rate answer-open. Derive only a coverage-valid diffuse-weight ATT corollary by nuclear/operator duality. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: the exact block identity Gamma_IQ=Gamma_IP Gamma_CP^dagger Gamma_CQ and balanced rank-one analysis suggest scale sigma sqrt(n), far below diameter n. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: matching tangent packing for every admissible wedge. EARLY KILL TEST: matching sigma_+ sqrt(n) bounds for the balanced rank-one L-mask.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Theorems 1--2 in Section 4.1, and Section 7
seed_details.proof_boundary: The published lower bound is scalar and genie-aided; the first changed step is a restriction-preserving Gaussian testing construction whose alternatives accumulate nuclear separation across the entire missing block.
seed_details.destination_search: A search for fixed-mask, known-rank, nuclear-norm confidence balls found trace-regression adaptation results and random-completion inference, but no deterministic L-mask result.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from entrywise instance-optimal intervals by summation.
seed_details.rebuttal: Summation loses the shared rank-one row and column directions and gives an order-\(n\) radius, whereas the proposed theorem targets order \(\sigma\sqrt n\) and requires a collective all-procedure lower bound.

seed_details.anchor_location: Algorithm 2, Section 4.2, and the leave-one-block-out discussion in Section 7
seed_details.proof_boundary: The published assembly is coordinatewise; the first changed step is joint singular-value control after synchronizing the cohortwise factor rotations.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing staggered adoption with a global nuclear confidence radius returned only entrywise, bilinear-functional, or random-mask uncertainty quantification.
seed_details.red_team: A triangle inequality over the published four-block intervals already gives the certificate.
seed_details.rebuttal: That construction pays with the number of cohorts and is not radius-comparable to the joint tangent modulus; the proposed certificate uses a single synchronized Gaussian spectral calculation.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Assumptions A--C, Proposition 2, and Section 6
seed_details.proof_boundary: Tall-wide factor transport uses strong factors in observed subblocks as a sufficient condition; the first changed step is constructing two wedges with controlled Gram spectra or proving a uniform tangent inverse bound.
seed_details.destination_search: No located deterministic-mask result makes finite overlap-Gram spectra an if-and-only-if invariant for honest nuclear uncertainty.
seed_details.red_team: The Gram eigenvalues merely restate the tall-wide strong-factor assumption.
seed_details.rebuttal: Sufficiency is implicit in block transport, but necessity for a global nuclear radius and completeness of this finite invariant across multi-cohort wedges are not established.

seed_details.seed: Joint nuclear-error limit law for four-block transport
seed_details.proof_boundary: The scalar Gaussian coupling must be replaced at the first projection step by a joint low-rank Gaussian matrix approximation and a singular-value delta method.
seed_details.destination_search: Random-mask debiasing papers give finite collections of entrywise or factor confidence regions, not a trace-norm limit under an L-mask.
seed_details.red_team: The continuous mapping theorem applied to the published Gaussian expansion gives the result.
seed_details.rebuttal: The expansion is entrywise rather than uniform in the growing missing block, and the nuclear norm is nondifferentiable at the shared low-rank Gaussian limit.

seed_details.seed: Known-rank nuclear efficiency bound under a deterministic wedge
seed_details.proof_boundary: The trace-regression likelihood has isotropic information; the first changed step is deriving the semiparametric tangent norm for a deterministic coordinate projection with a curved rank manifold.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found Bayesian Cram\'{e}r--Rao bounds for one missing entry, but no efficiency bound for the nonsmooth nuclear loss of a missing block.
seed_details.red_team: Nuclear loss has no regular influence function, so an efficiency bound is ill-posed.
seed_details.rebuttal: A local asymptotic minimax bound for the loss is meaningful, but the lack of a canonical regular scalar functional makes this lane less clean than the honest-radius formulation.

seed_details.seed: Conformal inversion of a low-rank counterfactual matrix path
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is finding a valid symmetry orbit for factor residual matrices under deterministic staggered missingness.
seed_details.destination_search: Counterfactual conformal methods use time permutations or placebo units, but the strong-factor model with independent cell noise already provides a more direct Gaussian route.
seed_details.red_team: Exact Gaussian noise makes conformal inversion an unnecessarily indirect calibration device.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the stated topic, which fixes the Gaussian experiment.

seed_details.anchor_location: Section 4 treatment-effect expansions, Proposition 4, and Section 6
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is optimizing the dual nuclear-ball radius against a direct functional influence variance over a class of weight matrices.
seed_details.destination_search: Direct ATT and bilinear-functional procedures occupy functional-specific optimality, while no paper located characterizes when one global nuclear ball is rate-competitive.
seed_details.red_team: Nuclear/operator duality makes the interval-length result immediate.
seed_details.rebuttal: Coverage transfer is immediate and is retained only as a corollary; statistical competitiveness against direct functional inference would require a separate lower bound and is not claimed as the kernel.
seed_details.disposition: dropped as kernel; retained as corollary

seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is replacing independent cohortwise rotation choices by one least-squares synchronization over the overlap graph.
seed_details.destination_search: No located staggered-panel theorem gives a global trace-norm guarantee without additive cohort accumulation.
seed_details.red_team: Rotation synchronization is standard multi-view PCA.
seed_details.rebuttal: Standard synchronization does not provide an observable honest radius or account for the anisotropic deterministic wedge, so it is a method component rather than a complete kernel.

seed_details.seed: Approximately low-rank honest nuclear oracle inequality
seed_details.proof_boundary: Their residual optimization treats worst-case Frobenius error of nuclear-norm minimization; the first changed step is separating approximation bias from stochastic nuclear uncertainty under uniform coverage.
seed_details.destination_search: The located result provides an asymptotic residual formula but not an honest random radius under the fixed factor geometry.
seed_details.red_team: Approximation bias can be appended to the exact-rank confidence radius.
seed_details.rebuttal: A uniformly estimable tail-nuclear bias is unavailable under the stated observations; this would require a new self-similarity or polished-tail condition and is outside the fixed-rank topic.

seed_details.seed: Adaptive adoption-policy regret from a global nuclear ball
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step would turn counterfactual uncertainty into a robust policy objective and analyze regret for future adoption assignments.
seed_details.destination_search: The anchor studies inference under a fixed realized adoption pattern, and the topic supplies neither a policy class nor a welfare functional.
seed_details.red_team: The policy object is absent from the model and would be grafted onto an inference problem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds under the fixed-adoption brief.
